A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DOPL/PREF-RMAB research. All 32 pages of each version, including Appendices A-F, are available and readable; text, equations, figures and tables support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulations comparing DOPL with baselines in App Marketing, CPAP and ARMMAN environments, plus CPAP estimation-error results (Figures 1-4).

after.justification: v2 retains the original simulation comparisons and CPAP estimation-error analysis in Figures 1-4 and Appendix F.

M1.justification: Sections 3 and Algorithms 2-3 retain the same transition confidence sets, Bradley-Terry preference estimation and inference, exploration bonus, and LP-derived index policy. Appendix C's extended LP and algorithm procedures are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same App Marketing, CPAP-adherence and ARMMAN-engagement simulations. Appendix B's sports-psychologist scenario remains a motivating example rather than an evaluated task.

E2.justification: Section 5 and Figures 1-3 retain the same comparators in all three environments: ORACLE, RANDOM, MLE_WIBQL, MLE_QWIC and MLE_LP. Their described procedures and comparison membership are unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix F retains the same arm counts, activation budgets, transition and reward specifications, and evaluation metrics. Tables 1-3 retain (K, H) settings of (4000, 100), (300, 1000) and (20000, 5), respectively, with epsilon 10^-5 throughout.

E4.justification: Appendix F.2.4 and Figure 4 retain the same CPAP analysis of index, preference, transition and reward estimation errors during training. No ablation, robustness test or other supplementary empirical analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Figures 1-4 preserve the same shaded bands. Neither version specifies repeated-run counts, seeds or the statistical meaning of those bands, and v2 adds no uncertainty-estimation procedure or significance test.

E6.justification: The four figure graphics are identical, retaining all episodic-reward, cumulative-regret and estimation-error curves. Section 5's findings about DOPL's performance relative to the learning baselines and oracle are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix E.2 adds episode-length factors H to the regret accounting and substantially revises the visit-count summation argument; E.3 revises the corresponding bound. v1 Lemmas 7-8 become v2 Lemmas 5-6 with doubled prefactors and N^2 replacing N under the square root. Theorem 1 doubles its displayed prefactors but retains N under the square root. Section 3.3 also newly states a uniform global attractor condition for asymptotic optimality. These are substantive changes to the central proof and its conditions, beyond lemma renumbering.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same core contributions: PREF-RMAB, direct online preference learning without explicit reward modeling, the first sublinear-regret guarantee for this setting, and empirical effectiveness. The introduction expands the regret expression and decomposition already presented in v1's theoretical section without changing these central claims.

C2.justification: Section 3.3 newly qualifies index-policy asymptotic optimality through the uniform global attractor condition. Section 2.2 adds a footnote suggesting action-dependent preferences to accommodate nonzero passive-arm rewards. The experimental interpretations and existing Limitations discussion are otherwise unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 5 replaces the anonymous experiment-code pointer with a named DOPL GitHub repository. Appendix F's embedded code link still points to the anonymous location. Hardware disclosures, hyperparameters and environment implementation details are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Gast, Gaujal and Yan (2024), citing it in Section 3.3 for the condition underlying index-policy asymptotic optimality. Appendix A and the broader positioning against dueling bandits, RLHF, DPO and standard RMAB research remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 expands the introduction's explanation of regret components, clarifies the occupancy-measure description, corrects some wording, and relabels the first two lemmas as propositions with subsequent renumbering. It also adds acknowledgments and conference-header text; the overall section and appendix organization is retained.

P2.justification: The conference header and local reflow alter text placement and equation breaks, including moving the start of Appendix F from page 28 to page 29. All four figures and three tables retain their designs, axes, legends, captions and content.

improvement.justification: v2 makes an optimality condition explicit and adds more detailed regret accounting. However, the revised component bounds and Appendix E derivations use N^2 under the square root, while Theorem 1 and retained appendix bound statements still use N. These revisions leave the central proof and stated guarantee unreconciled. The useful clarifications coexist with newly exposed internal mismatches, so the PDFs do not establish a reliable net improvement in overall quality.
